reason: A is the better proposal because it specifies an alloy state, processing schedule, testing conditions, baseline, and clear falsification criterion, whereas B leaves cooling rates, aging parameters, and phase selection undefined and invokes unsupported transformation-induced plasticity. A still has major weaknesses—especially the questionable expectation that grain refinement improves ductility and that aging raises Young’s modulus by 10–20%, plus its lack of high-temperature testing—but it is more directly testable and methodologically actionable.
